name: ship
subject: E04's galleon. Three clay concepts staged 2026-08-03 at E:/AI/training/facet_next/galleon_clay/galleon_clay_p1_{00004,00005,00006}.png. NOT YET DESIGNATED - which of the three is the ship is the Director's call at E04 Gate 0.
provenance: DRAFT, written 2026-08-04 (E04 Task 2) from the stressor table in docs/profiles-design.md. Nothing here has textured anything. Values are marked measured / inherited-pending-review / SUSPENDED, and a SUSPENDED value must be derived on this subject before the stage that reads it runs.
_status: DRAFT - DO NOT RUN A TEXTURE PASS FROM THIS FILE. Its purpose is to make explicit, before E04 starts, which character values a ship must NOT inherit. Several entries are deliberately absent rather than guessed; their absence is the finding the design note asked for.

_what_was_measured_and_what_could_not_be.frame_aspect_MEASURED: All three staged concepts are 1216 x 1024 = 1.188 W/H. That is a fact about the staged images and it is measured, not assumed.
_what_was_measured_and_what_could_not_be.subject_bbox_NOT_MEASURABLE_YET: The subject's own aspect could not be measured from the concepts. A corner-median key over all four corners returns the FULL FRAME as the subject bbox on all three (fill 64.2% / 67.5% / 79.3%), because these are clay renders on a soft gradient with a cast shadow - the exact configuration this repo has recorded failing three times (E01's painted concept, the Workbench grey-on-grey render, the diffusion studio backdrop). Keying was not retried with a different threshold; where geometry can answer the question, geometry answers it. The subject aspect is therefore SUSPENDED until Task 3's reconstructed mesh exists, and is then read off the mesh bbox.
_what_was_measured_and_what_could_not_be.why_this_matters: The design note's stressor table predicts fit_axis width and a landscape frame. The frame is landscape and that is confirmed. Whether the MESH is wider than tall - which is what fit_axis actually keys off - is not established by a landscape frame, and this file will not assert it.

palette.why: On this subject the off-palette gate carries weight nobody's eye can: no one knows by sight what a galleon's palette should be. It must be authored from the galleon's named materials and cross-checked against a DIFFERENT image than the twins it will gate, or it is a tautology. The character's W3 palette must never be pointed at a ship - its bands cover a red beard, gold pauldrons and a green knitted tunic.
palette.owner: the advisor, after the Director designates

twin_prompts.why: Identity belongs to the prompt. A ship's named elements - hull planking, ratlines, stern-castle carving, sail cloth - reach the image only if the prompt names them.

brush_prompts.why: Per-view, same reason as the character's.

mesh_gate.why: gate_mesh.py's head/shoulder logic is meaningless on a ship. Recorded as an explicit 'none' rather than silently not running it, so a future session sees a decision instead of an omission.

head_rect_metrics.why: There is no face rect, so mesh_stats' face-rect density and curvature columns have no referent. mesh_stats still measures shell count and density, which it does identically on any mesh.

reg_iou_min.why: The character's 0.80 was derived from BOTH SIDES of a measured line on W3's twins - adjudicated 0.8329-0.9533 against failures at or below 0.578. A galleon has neither distribution yet. Inheriting 0.80 would be inheriting one subject's spread as another's threshold, which is the exact error the withdrawn off-palette percentage made. Derive from this subject's own twins or run with the halt suspended and REPORT the IoU per view.
reg_iou_min.from: E08 Amendment 27; CLAUDE.md 'suspend rather than invent one'

bbox_tol.why: 0.25 is W3 data, and it is already demoted to a diagnostic on the character because figure area swings 1.65x with camera geometry. A ship's swing between a bow-on view and a broadside is far larger than a human's between profile and three-quarter. Do not inherit.

crop-res.why: Frame convention for whatever rect this subject privileges, if any. Carried so the unit is explicit even before a rect exists.

tag.why: Filename stem for this subject's silhouettes.

_ABSENT_ON_PURPOSE.framing (aspect, render w/h, fit axis, t: SUSPENDED. The staged frame is 1216x1024; the mesh's own extents decide fit_axis and the margin, and no mesh exists. Guessing here is how a character default reaches a ship.
_ABSENT_ON_PURPOSE.allocation (crop rect, head-scale, targe: SUSPENDED. Every one of these presumes a privileged region. A galleon may have one - the stern castle, where the carved detail is - but it has not been chosen, and 'anchor: none' is an equally legitimate answer that the design note lists first.
_ABSENT_ON_PURPOSE.cameras (production set, step, elevated: SUSPENDED, and it is a real design question rather than a transcription. Decks need looking INTO; the character's +55 elevated pair was chosen to see a crown and boot-tops. A ship may need a mast-head down-angle and a low bow-on that no character ever needed.
_ABSENT_ON_PURPOSE.thin_policy (thin-extent): SUSPENDED, and this is the sharpest stressor in the whole file. 0.030 was the smallest value that fills a GREATSWORD solid. Ratlines, shrouds and stays are far thinner than a blade - visible in all three staged concepts as single-pixel lines - so the character value is not merely unportable, it is wrong by an order of magnitude in a direction that would hand the entire rigging to the diffusion brush. Measure the rigging's extent on the designated mesh before choosing.
_ABSENT_ON_PURPOSE.acceptance (facing floors, edge-dist fam: SUSPENDED. edge-ref 700.0 is literally one character's figure width in twin pixels used as a denominator. A ship's twin-pixel width is a different number and the erosion scales off it.
_ABSENT_ON_PURPOSE.generation recipe (seed, steps, cfg, den: SUSPENDED pending E04's own anchor. The character's recipe was validated against the character's twins; a hull under a style LoRA trained on figures is an open question, not an inherited setting.
